extension.description: Nine protocol decoders, X-trace, waveform diff, FSM views and switching activity on VCD/FST/GHW — in an editor tab, cross-probing LintCrux, SimCrux and NetCrux over CXP.
crux.command.sendSelectionToPeer.title: Send Selection to Crux App
crux.configuration.title: EDACrux
crux.configuration.crossProbe.revealSele: Bring the matching editor tab forward when a connected Crux app announces a selection. Keyboard focus stays where it is and the window is never raised.
crux.configuration.crossProbe.openSource: Move the cursor into the editor when a connected Crux app asks to open a source location. The window itself is never raised.
crux.command.wavecrux.openPanel.title: Open Waveform Panel
crux.command.openCapabilitiesPanel.title: Open Capabilities Panel
crux.command.toggleRtlAnnotation.title: Toggle RTL Value Annotation
crux.configuration.rtlAnnotation.enabled: Render signal values from the connected waveform as inline decorations in your Verilog/VHDL source, following the waveform cursor. Off by default; only stems-exact matches are annotated, and an ambiguous name is shown as ambiguous rather than guessed.
crux.untrustedWorkspaces.description: Waveforms open, decode and cross-probe normally here: this extension only reads the files you open and never runs a program. A workspace setting that switches on inline RTL value annotation is ignored, because an untrusted folder should not put text into your source — switch it on in your own settings, or trust the folder.
crux.configuration.crossProbe.followWave: Reveal a signal's RTL declaration in the editor when you select it in a WaveCrux waveform panel in this window. Off by default: most clicks in a waveform are reading, not a request to navigate. Resolved through the stems index, so it lands only on declarations a tool wrote down; keyboard focus stays in the waveform.
